subject: RetailCo: Spike in 429/504 after Model v5 int8 rollout
messages:
From: Marta Ruiz <marta.ruiz@retailco.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops@retailco.com
Date: 2027-05-09T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Model v5 rollout: spike in 429/504 errors and timeouts

Hi Irene,

We started seeing a sharp increase in 429/504 responses and client timeouts on the product_search route around 06:05 PT this morning—right after the model v5 int8 variant was promoted to 30% of requests. Error rate climbed from ~0.3% to ~8% at peak, and tail latency (p95/p99) doubled. Retries from our front-end made the problem worse (retry storms).

Attached are a trimmed set of server logs and a representative request body. The failures are concentrated on queries with long contexts (user history + filters). We rollbacked our client-side retries temporarily but still see spike in error responses from your side.

This is impacting our checkout search funnel; we need a mitigation plan and ETA. We are open to a rollback to the previous model if that is the fastest route. Please advise with urgency — we will need an update to our Executive team within the hour.

Thanks,
Marta Ruiz
Head of Product Operations
RetailCo

Attachments: logs_20270509.zip (trimmed), sample_request.json
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marta Ruiz <marta.ruiz@retailco.com>
Date: 2027-05-09T09:28:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Model v5 rollout: spike in 429/504 errors and timeouts

Thanks Marta — sorry you're seeing this. Copying the on-call infra and kernel team. Initial triage from our side:

- Symptom: elevated 429/5xx and increased p99 latency concentrated on product_search route after model-v5-int8 promotion at ~06:00 PT.
- Hypothesis: recent int8 quantization profile + new kernel selection for int8 matmul could be yielding correctness/perf regressions on long-context batches, causing per-request CPU/GPU stalls and increased retry surface.

Immediate mitigations (pick one; we should act quickly):
1) Emergency rollback: revert traffic for RetailCo to model-v4-fp16 (fastest to remove regression).
2) Traffic split change: reduce v5-int8 from 30% -> 0% for RetailCo (pin routing policy).
3) Kernel fallback: force-vendor-kernel=fallback (slower but stable) for v5-int8 on affected nodes.
4) Client-side: request RetailCo disable aggressive retries (they already started this).

Jonas/Hannah — can you validate whether pinned kernel fallback is safe to flip immediately and the expected latency delta? If rollback is needed, Marissa can you prepare an exec brief and get sign-off for emergency rollback and a small service credit? I'll prepare a short customer-facing note.

I attached a short initial-analysis.txt capturing process.

—Irene
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

Attachment: initial-analysis.txt
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-09T09:45:00-07:00
Subject: Executive brief: RetailCo modelv5-induced retry storms (need approval)

Rishi — escalating to you because RetailCo is threatening to pause their expansion commit if we can't restore stable performance within the hour. Short summary:

- Impact: RetailCo product_search route 429/504 spike; customer-facing revenue funnel impact. Estimated affected requests: ~12k/min during peak.
- Root cause (working hypothesis): performance regression introduced by model-v5 int8 rollout and new kernel selection on T4/GPU fleet for long-context requests.
- Proposed immediate action (requires approval): 1) Emergency rollback for RetailCo traffic to model-v4-fp16 (rollback window ~5 minutes), 2) Offer 10% service credit for the incident window, 3) Launch postmortem and slow re-rollout with extra canary checks.
- Ask: Approve emergency rollback + 10% credit and allocate SRE time for next 48 hours to stabilize.

Customer update to send once approved: brief apology, mitigation steps, ETA to full restoration, and commitment to root-cause timeline.

Irene/Jonas/Hannah — please keep logs and perf diffs in the Drive folder linked in this thread.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
VP, Customer Success
Redwood Inference
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, Marta Ruiz <marta.ruiz@retailco.com>
Date: 2027-05-09T10:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Executive brief: RetailCo modelv5-induced retry storms (need approval)

Quick tech notes from kernel/serving triage:

- We reproduced the issue on a T4 replica: the int8 matmul kernel selected by the new kernel-selector path shows a pathological slow path for sequences >1024 with heavy KV cache churn. This increases per-token compute by ~18-25% for the affected batch shapes, which cascades into service retries upstream.
- The quantization profile exposed a subtle numerical instability for a subset of attention heads when paired with that kernel; we see rare correctness anomalies that trigger downstream error handling in the model runtime, manifesting as 504/timeouts on our endpoint.

Safe mitigations we can push now:
1) Pin RetailCo routing to model-v4-fp16 (recommended) — rollback window minimal, immediate customer restoration expected.
2) If rollback approval delayed: flip kernel selector to force-fallback-kernel on the affected pool (adds ~10-12% latency but eliminates correctness anomalies).
3) Preventive: Add a canary check that runs long-context queries through the selected kernel+quant profile pre-promote (will add to our rollout gating).

I'll prepare a one-click rollback and the kernel-fallback toggle. Marissa — you have approval: confirm and I'll execute. If Rishi prefers, we can kick off rollback now and follow up with credit details.

On discovery notes: this is model-variant specific (v5-int8 + kernel combo). Rebuilding the quant profile with stricter calibration reduces the risk but will take 2-3 days for validation.

Jonas Weber
Head of Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
